newsitem.title: MEXICO: Family gather at bedside of frail Mexican labor boss.
newsitem.headline: Family gather at bedside of frail Mexican labor boss.

text.p: Relatives of the powerful Mexican labour boss Fidel Velazquez were called to his hospital bedside as the 97-year-old leader's health lapsed, media reported on Friday.

"He is in a very delicate state of health," TV network Televisa's anchorman Guillermo Ortega said. ""He had a lapse and his family were urgently called to his bedside. It is important to point out that the relatives were urgently called out last (Thursday) night."
Daily Reforma reported on Friday that Velazquez was in "intensive care" in the Presidential Guard Hospital, a military hospital in Mexico City.

Velazquez has been a pillar of the long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), swinging labour support behind the government for 60 years as leader of the Confederation of Mexican Workers (CTM), now 6 million strong.
Velaquez's doctor Salomon Jasqui told reporters late on Thursday that Velazquez's condition was stable.
"He's now stable, he's perfectly well, and he has improved considerably," Dr. Salomon Jasqui told reporters on leaving the hospital. "He's sleeping now."
On Wednesday, Jasqui told reporters Velazquez's temperature rose to 100 degrees (38 celsius) and that his levels of potasium and sodium were dangerously low.
Velazquez has been in and out of the hospital several times in recent months and last entered the hospital on June 5 with what Jasqui described as a urinary infection.
